To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the G proteins that modulate the activity of adenylyll cyclase in mouse brain undergo developmental changes in expression and function.
the G protein subunits that modulate adenyylcyclase activity in mouse cerebral cortex undergo developmental changes in their relative abundance.
the G proteins that modulate adenyylcyclase activity in mouse forebrain undergo developmental changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression and regulation of the G proteins that differentiate between the adenylyl‐cyclase activating Gs and the inhibitory Gs and Go subfamilies.
the developmental expression of G proteins and their role in the regulation of the adenylyl cylcase system.
the expression of G proteins during mouse brain development.

Gs, Gi1 and Go are expressed in the prenatal brain, whereas Gi2 and Go are expressed postnatally, with Gpp[NHp] stimulated adenylyr cyclase activity being maximal postnatally.
the G proteins that modulate adenyyl cyclase activity are developmentally expressed in mouse brain.
the G protein α family is expressed in a highly complex pattern in the brain during development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gs, Gi1 and Go subunits were present prenatally and that the Gi2 subunit was expressed postnatally.
the G protein α and β subunit expression is developmentally regulated.
Gi1 is the most abundant G protein in the brain, that Gi2 is the most effective GTPase and Gi2 is the major G protein that mediates the inhibition of adenyyll cyclase.

G proteins are present in the brain before birth and that they are developmentally regulated.
